name: Whole units, losses and converter loops

pages.text: Conversions must not round a tiny offer up into free power. The long-valued bridges move exact representable quanta; a remainder stays in its original storage instead of being invented or silently claimed as transferred.$p$(l)Illustrative arithmetic, not a server setting$()$p2.5 J per FE, no loss — 5 J converts to 2 FE; a smaller offer can be insufficient.$p2.5 J per FE, 10% input loss — 25 J converts to 9 FE.$p4 FE per EU, 10% input loss — 100 EU becomes 360 FE.$pSame ratio, then 20% output loss — Those 360 FE become 72 EU.$pInput and output losses are independent, but the bridge uses one base ratio. Very precise ratios can require a large quantum. If that quantum exceeds the transfer rate or remaining buffer space, transfer pauses. That is not necessarily a broken cable.$pGT block packets are rounded conservatively at packet boundaries, rather than using a fictional simulated packet API. Fractional AE item operations also use conservative rounding. No simulation is supposed to debit storage.$p$(o)A safe round trip inside Calculator does not prove an entire modpack is free of converter loops. Another mod can use a different exchange rate. Prefer inherit, align all converters, or deliberately close incompatible routes. Changing rates with charged buffers changes their native-equivalent value; it does not rewrite stored FE.$()$p$(l:foundations_calculator:power/eu_conversion)Read the actual server ratios$()
